title: Per-agent identity & delegation on every action (SPIFFE, OAuth token exchange, MCP auth, IETF agent drafts)
outcome: A recommended scheme that binds every action to one agent identity, through delegation chains and shared tools, and can be revoked fast
acceptance: ≥5 primary sources with URLs (specs/RFCs/drafts with version: SPIFFE, RFC 8693, MCP authorization spec, draft-klrc-aiagent-auth, RFC 9421 or similar)
Table comparing ≥4 approaches on: granularity (workload vs action), delegation chain support, non-repudiation, revocation latency, prototype effort
Explicit analysis of where attribution collapses (shared MCP server / service credentials) and how to keep it
'Implications for our design' section with a recommended identity + action-signing scheme for Identity and Containment
summary: Correction: 12 primary sources (not 13). Workload identity (SPIFFE/WIMSE) identifies a process, not an action; RFC 8693 treats prior actors in an act chain as informational only; MCP forbids token passthrough so upstream APIs see the MCP server, not the agent, which is where attribution collapses. SPIRE docs read show short TTLs (1h X.509, 5m JWT) and node ban but no SVID revocation. klrc-03 (Jul 2026) is the live IETF draft; txn-tokens-for-agents-05 and pedigree-00 are expired single-author drafts; none defines fast revocation alone. Top design implication: SPIFFE-format agent ID + RFC 8693-style act chain + per-agent Ed25519 signed action record, all via a tool gateway that writes the record and holds a deny-list (immediate containment), with short TTLs bounding the rest.
